sourceItem.promptActual:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one entirely NEW square present-day documentary photograph for Matkakirja. Reference 1 gives only the real Tivoli Musikkarrusellen architecture; reference 2 gives only the fictional Freja identity. Do not edit or reuse the old composition.
The viewer is a traveler standing immediately at the entrance of the stationary carousel at closing time. Freja is right beside its small access gate, with the cream-and-gold canopy, carved horses, brass poles and a little of the real upper gallery close behind her. A small family of three visitors is walking off the ride behind her, visibly human at a believable nearby scale, with slight natural walking blur. No remote lake or distant carousel.
Freja is the same ordinary 31-year-old Danish attendant: heavily freckled pale angular face, auburn hair in two untidy braids, worn forest-green work coveralls, white T-shirt, burgundy waist pouch. She has been turning a key in the gate lock, and suddenly turns her face toward the lens when the traveler asks about a treasure. BOTH eyes look directly into the camera. Her expression is arrested between stern 'we are closed' and surprised incredulous amusement: one eyebrow lifts while the other remains drawn down, lips slightly parted with just one corner beginning to rise. A compelling spontaneous human reaction, no posed grin. One hand holds the key naturally in the gate lock; the other rests loosely on the gate, both fully visible and anatomically simple.
Eye-level 35 mm environmental photograph, camera about 1.5 metres away. Upper thighs through whole head visible, the face prominent but with breathing room around the hair and hands. Freja slightly off-center so the departing people and horses tell a second small story. A credible candid photograph taken with gentle fill flash at early dusk: pale neutral Nordic skin, soft grey-blue ambient light, modest warm practical carousel bulbs. Expose the background clearly. Moderate depth of field so the nearby architecture and people remain recognizable; quiet lens rendering, no decorative bokeh. Real cotton wrinkles, unretouched skin and modest imperfections in painted wood. Soft photographic detail and restrained contrast, no artificial sharpening, HDR, cinematic teal-orange grading, waxy skin, CGI or illustration texture. No border, fading, watermark, captions, or readable invented lettering. Keep critical details within the central 84 percent for later edge treatment.

sourceItem.promptActual:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: Matkakirja game location photograph
Primary request: Create a completely new, ordinary documentary travel photograph of Ale's Stones (Ales stenar) at Kåseberga in Skåne, Sweden, using the supplied authentic photograph as the strict site and geometry reference.
Input image: reference photograph of the actual surviving monument; preserve the real stone arrangement.
Scene/backdrop: the existing 67-metre ship-shaped setting of large upright weathered stones on a low open coastal grass ridge, with a restrained glimpse of the Baltic Sea and flat Skåne horizon.
Subject: the full curving double row of standing stones must read clearly as a stone ship; larger end stones and irregular natural stone sizes, spacing, lean and surfaces.
Style/medium: believable contemporary documentary photograph, natural optics and surfaces, modest consumer full-frame camera, slightly soft lens rendering, realistic dynamic range and depth.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2, human eye level from just inside or beside one end, strong depth along both rows, monument fills most of frame, limited empty sky.
Lighting/mood: calm cool Nordic daylight with thin clouds and gentle shadows; no dramatic sunset.
Constraints: keep the real location, low terrain, coastline relationship and monument geometry recognizably faithful to the reference; no people, signs, paths dominating, text, watermark, invented ruins.
Avoid: CGI, painting, fantasy, HDR, oversaturation, hyper-sharpening, perfect repeated stones, extra monuments, aerial view.

Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: Matkakirja location image
Primary request: Create a completely new contemporary documentary photograph of the real Urnes Stave Church at Ornes, using the supplied authentic photograph as strict architecture and setting reference.
Scene: the small dark timber church in its grassy graveyard on the steep green slope above Lustrafjorden; quiet Norwegian summer day.
Composition: ordinary standing eye-level three-quarter exterior view, landscape frame, whole church readable with modest fjord and mountain context; natural imperfect travel-photo framing.
Style: believable camera photograph, soft overcast daylight, restrained dynamic range, uneven natural sharpness, weathered dark wood and roof shingles.
Accuracy: preserve the authentic church silhouette, compact tower and spire, real roof junctions, porch, graveyard and fjord slope. The long side wall must remain predominantly plain, very dark weathered vertical timber. Any historic carved boards must be narrow, low-contrast, shadowed, subtle and subordinate exactly as in the reference; do not create bright, broad, repeated or full-height decorative panels.
Avoid: extra ornament, repeated knotwork panels, fantasy stave-church features, altered roof tiers, CGI, painting, HDR, microcontrast, plastic wood, dramatic light, people, text, watermark.
